answer: We prove Sybil resistance through a zero-knowledge verifiable delay function where the consensus kernel relies on dynamic opportunity-cost bonds. When an adversary attempts identity multiplication, a subgame-perfect punishment matrix triggers automated slashing of this staking collateral. Since this ferrous constraint renders the expected utility of attack strictly negative, the protocol converges to a unique, robust Nash equilibrium, securing the distributed ledger as a highly resilient orchard of cryptoeconomic validations.
